title: The Wonderful City of Oz, part 5
attribution: From The Wonderful Wizard of Oz by L. Frank Baum (1900), via Project Gutenberg, in reading order.
body: It was not such an awful voice as she had expected to come from the big Head; so she took courage and answered:
“I am Dorothy, the Small and Meek. I have come to you for help.”
The eyes looked at her thoughtfully for a full minute. Then said the voice:
“Where did you get the silver shoes?”
“I got them from the Wicked Witch of the East, when my house fell on her and killed her,” she replied.
“Where did you get the mark upon your forehead?” continued the voice.
“That is where the Good Witch of the North kissed me when she bade me good-bye and sent me to you,” said the girl.
Again the eyes looked at her sharply, and they saw she was telling the truth. Then Oz asked, “What do you wish me to do?”

“Send me back to Kansas, where my Aunt Em and Uncle Henry are,” she answered earnestly. “I don’t like your country, although it is so beautiful. And I am sure Aunt Em will be dreadfully worried over my being away so long.”

The eyes winked three times, and then they turned up to the ceiling and down to the floor and rolled around so queerly that they seemed to see every part of the room. And at last they looked at Dorothy again.
“Why should I do this for you?” asked Oz.
“Because you are strong and I am weak; because you are a Great Wizard and I am only a little girl.”
“But you were strong enough to kill the Wicked Witch of the East,” said Oz.
“That just happened,” returned Dorothy simply; “I could not help it.”

“Well,” said the Head, “I will give you my answer. You have no right to expect me to send you back to Kansas unless you do something for me in return. In this country everyone must pay for everything he gets. If you wish me to use my magic power to send you home again you must do something for me first. Help me and I will help you.”

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how does Dorothy name herself to Oz?
options: Dorothy, the Small and Meek
Dorothy of Kansas
The Sorceress of the East
Dorothy, the Great and Terrible

questions.prompt: Per the passage, where did Dorothy say she got the silver shoes?
options: From the Wicked Witch of the East, killed by her house
From the Good Witch of the North as a parting gift
From the Munchkins who made them for her
From the green girl at the palace

questions.prompt: According to the passage, where did the mark on her forehead come from?
options: The Good Witch of the North's kiss
The Wicked Witch's dying blow
The Guardian's locked spectacles
The fall of the house

questions.prompt: Per the passage, what does Dorothy ask Oz to do?
options: Send her back to Kansas to her aunt and uncle
Give her a way to cross the great desert
Make the Munchkins stop calling her a witch
Take the silver shoes away from her

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does Oz say everyone must do in that country?
options: Pay for everything he gets
Obey the Wizard without question
Wear green spectacles at all times
Serve a year in the palace

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why was Dorothy able to take courage?
options: The voice was not as awful as she had expected
The Head smiled kindly at her as she came in
The green girl had come in with her after all
She could see the Wizard was only pretending

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what convinced Oz that Dorothy spoke honestly?
options: His eyes looked at her sharply and saw she told the truth
The soldier had vouched for her beforehand
She showed him the mark on her forehead
She refused to claim any credit for the killing

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, how does Dorothy explain killing the Witch of the East?
options: That it simply happened and she could not help it
That the silver shoes had done it for her
That the Good Witch of the North had arranged it
That she had meant to do it all along

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does Dorothy mean by calling herself meek?
options: Small and without power of her own
Quiet because she is frightened
Patient in waiting for an answer
Modest about what she has done

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the passage?
options: A plea for help is answered with a demand for payment first
A plea for help is granted at once by a kindly wizard
A wizard proves that Dorothy has been lying to him
A girl refuses to tell the Wizard where she came from

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how long did the eyes look at her before speaking?
options: A full minute
Only an instant
Half an hour
They never looked at her

questions.prompt: Per the passage, how many times did the eyes wink?
options: Three
Once
Five
They did not wink

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what reason does Dorothy give for Oz helping her?
options: He is strong and a great wizard, and she is only a little girl
She has already killed one wicked witch for him
The Good Witch of the North sent her to him
She will pay him with the silver shoes

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what does Dorothy say about the Land of Oz?
options: That she does not like it, beautiful though it is
That she would gladly stay if Aunt Em could come
That it is far better than Kansas ever was
That she has seen too little of it to judge

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what does Oz point out about Dorothy's own strength?
options: That she was strong enough to kill the Witch of the East
That she walked the whole way from Munchkin country
That she faced the Kalidahs without running
That she alone dared ask to see him

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does earnestly convey about Dorothy's answer?
options: She spoke with serious feeling
She spoke in a great hurry
She spoke without much hope
She spoke to flatter him

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarises the passage?
options: A truthful account wins a hearing, but help is made conditional
A wizard sends a girl away without listening to her
A girl bargains successfully for a journey home
A wizard admits he has no magic power at all
